commentary_segments.text: As an opamp a symmetrical OTA is used. Current starving is used however, to increase the gain (see Chapter 7). At such a low supply voltage, too little room is available for cascodes. Current starving means that a DC current source takes away most of the DC current from the load transistors M2. As a result, the AC impedance of these transistors increase, giving rise to more gain. A large factor B is used as well. The first amplifier of this sigma-delta converter uses a k value of 0.8 and a B factor of 10. Actually, factor k indicates what fraction of the current through the input transistor M1 is taken up by the DC current source. The small-signal resistance 1/g of transistors M2 increases m2 by a factor (1−k) in weak inversion, and so does the small-signal gain A.
